items.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence in enterprise settings has ushered in a new era characterized by foundation models, federated learning, and secure cloud-based architectures. Foundation models, pre-trained on massive datasets, enable enterprises to leverage generalized AI capabilities across diverse applications, from natural language processing and computer vision to predictive analytics. However, the deployment of such large-scale AI systems introduces significant challenges, including computational demands, data privacy concerns, model interpretability, and operational scalability. Federated learning has emerged as a promising solution to mitigate privacy risks by enabling decentralized model training without centralizing sensitive enterprise data, thereby supporting collaboration across departments or organizations while maintaining regulatory compliance. Concurrently, secure cloud systems provide the infrastructure necessary to scale AI deployments efficiently while implementing robust security mechanisms such as encryption, identity-based access control, and Zero Trust principles. This paper explores strategies for integrating foundation models, federated learning, and secure cloud architectures within enterprise AI frameworks, highlighting best practices for MLOps, governance, auditing, and risk management. It also addresses the organizational, technical, and regulatory challenges associated with nextgeneration AI adoption and proposes frameworks to operationalize AI responsibly and securely. By synthesizing insights from distributed AI architectures, cloud-native infrastructures, and ethical AI principles, this study provides a roadmap for enterprises seeking to deploy AI systems that are not only scalable and efficient but also secure, privacy-preserving, and compliant with evolving regulatory standards.</jats:p>
title: Next-Generation Enterprise AI: From Foundation Models to Federated and Secure Cloud Systems

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Abstract
This manuscript presents a comprehensive academic framework for understanding how foundation models, vision transformers, and multimodal artificial intelligence are transforming predictive diagnostics and biomedical discovery in next-generation precision healthcare. The text is organized as a monograph that moves from conceptual foundations and uncertainty-aware research design to statistical explanation, causal reasoning, trustworthy machine learning, reproducible analytics engineering, and policy-sensitive implementation. The central argument is that healthcare AI should not be reduced to isolated predictive tasks; rather, it must be understood as a layered ecosystem in which representation learning, evidence standards, workflow discipline, institutional capacity, and governance accountability co-evolve. Throughout the manuscript, emphasis is placed on globally relevant research pathways that can operate across diverse infrastructures in South Asia, Europe, Africa, and the Americas. The book therefore combines theoretical reasoning with methodological frameworks, deployment logic, and governance models suited to doctoral scholarship, professional practice, and strategic policy design. Its contribution lies in integrating computational sophistication with translational realism, enabling researchers and institutions to design precision-health systems that are analytically rigorous, operationally reproducible, ethically defensible, and scalable across heterogeneous care environments.
Keywords
foundation models, vision transformers, multimodal AI, precision healthcare, predictive diagnostics, medical imaging, clinical inference, biomedical discovery, causal inference, explainability, trustworthiness, uncertainty quantification, digital health, wearable biosensing, omics analytics, healthcare MLOps, reproducibility, governance, translational AI, health policy, representation learning, diagnostic medicine</jats:p>
title: Foundation Models, Vision Transformers, and Multimodal AI for Next-Generation Precision Healthcare

items.abstract: <jats:p>Next-generation networks (NGNs) face growing demands for more bandwidth, lower delay, and better intelligence. Foundation Models (FMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful generative artificial intelligence models that could help meet these demands. However, there is confusion about their differences and how best to use them in NGNs. This research survey presents a detailed evaluation of FMs against LLMs to illustrate the distinct characteristics and benefits of both models. The work also examines NGN applications, which include network traffic analysis enhancement and network management automation, as well as security improvement through the use of these models. The research paper discusses vital enabling techniques that are needed to train and customize the current models. Research results show that NGNs experience improved intelligent operations through the use of FMs together with LLMs. The process of implementing FMs and LLMs, along with their training, encounters obstacles that include demanding data as well as high computational expenses and security issues. The study emphasizes that future NGNs require FMs and LLMs to succeed; yet, further studies are necessary to overcome existing obstacles and reach their complete capabilities.</jats:p>
title: Foundation Models and Large Language Models in Next Generation Networks: Comparison, Opportunities and Challenges
